title: Granular ask atelier and probe blueprints — Jun 2029
summary: Working synthesis of recent customer feedback across pilot accounts. This doc stitches micro-asks into grouped hypothesis lanes and proposes lightweight probe blueprints (MVP experiments) to validate effort vs impact. Focus areas: latency tolerance windows, onboarding friction for Private deploys, model-fallback transparency, and per-route cost visibility.
themes: Latency and tail SLOs: customers report unpredictable tails at 95-99th percentiles when batching spikes are present
Private onboarding friction: network/K8s config, KMS onboarding and image validation steps are tripping first-10-day installs
Observability granularity: request-level traces lack token-level cost attribution and KV-cache hit visibility
Model-fallback and quality drift: side-by-side fallback decisions feel opaque to platform teams
Cost controls: customers want per-route soft limits and clearer guidance on batching vs latency tradeoffs
priority_requests: Expose KV-cache hit/miss metric per model-version and prefix key range (high impact for recommender and chat workloads)
Add 'canary latency window' config to rollouts so customers can test rollout speed vs latency SLOs
Private: provide a one-click KMS key-provisioning checklist and validation utility for common clouds
Per-route budget alarms (USD/day) with automated fallback to cheaper model-variants
Developer debugging mode that returns anonymized prefix+KV-cache snapshots for failing requests
probe_plans: KV-cache visibility probe: instrument 3 pilot tenants for 2 weeks, surface hit/miss rates, link to infra autoscale events; short survey after 2 weeks
Canary-latency toggle: roll out toggle to Dedicated customers on t-shirt sizes M/L, observe 95th percentile impact during predictable traffic windows
Onboard checklist microflow: script a guided runbook for 5 pilot customers using Private; measure time-to-first-successful-inference and number of support touchpoints
Per-route budget experiment: enable soft budget on two customers, configure automated fallback and collect app-level error rates and user-reported regressions
Developer debug flag: add ephemeral flag for 48-hour window on support tickets; capture anonymized KV fragments and attach to ticket
acceptance_criteria: KV-cache probe: show >=20% delta in per-customer per-model token cost attributable to cache misses vs baseline
Canary-latency toggle: customers can configure window and observe <10% increase in P50 while reducing 95th by measurable percent during test
Onboard checklist: reduce time-to-first-successful-inference by >=30% for Private pilots
Per-route budget: automated fallback reduces overbudget errors by >=75% and maintains application-availability >99%
Debug flag: support team able to triage 60% of flagged tickets without requiring full repro environment
risks_and_blockers: Instrumentation cost: adding token-level metrics will increase telemetry volume and storage costs
Privacy: storing any prefix or KV content requires strict anonymization and legal review for regulated customers
Rollback complexity: automated fallback introduces risk of quality regressions for critical flows
Resource contention: Dedicated pools may need temporary resizing for canary-latency tests
Cross-team bandwidth: requires coordination across serving-runtime, infra, and product to deliver usable dashboards

customer_quotes: "We can tolerate a little extra P50 if the 99th tail doesn't spike — it's the surprise outages that break SLAs." — large marketplace infra team
"Private install took us longer than expected because the KMS step failed silently; we had to re-run and escalate." — regulated finance customer
"If the platform could tell us when a model fallback happened and why, our app could surface a message to end-users instead of 500s." — customer success engineer at a chatbot vendor
"Seeing token-level cost per route would let us attribute spend to features rather than teams. Right now it's a black box." — platform engineering manager
recommended_actions: Kick off KV-cache probe immediately with two high-volume chat pilots and one recommender tenant; limit telemetry retention to 14 days for probe
Design 'canary latency window' config and prototype UI in Console for rollout controls (small toggle + analytics card)
Build an opinionated Private onboarding runbook and small CLI validator for common KMS/cloud combos; include automated tests for image and network reachability
Prototype per-route soft budgets as a beta feature behind a flag and document fallback quality expectations
Scope a privacy review for debug snapshots; draft anonymization rules and legal checklist before enabling debug-flag for regulated tenants
open_questions: What is the acceptable telemetry cost threshold for token-level metrics before product decides to limit to sampled traces?
Can fallback decisions include model-quality scores at runtime without exposing model internals?
Which Private customers are willing to participate in 2-week probes that collect anonymized KV metrics?
What SLAs do we guarantee if per-route budgets trigger automatic fallback?
Do we need a dedicated compliance path for debug-flag captures in EU-regulated customers?
next_steps: Schedule 30-min sync with serving-runtime, infra, and product to align probe instrumentation (owner: Ravi) — target by 2029-06-20
Recruit 3 pilot accounts (CS outreach) and secure opt-in consent for anonymized telemetry (owner: Aisha) — target by 2029-06-24
Create a lightweight Confluence page with runbook templates and add to linked_artifacts (owner: Helena) — target by 2029-06-21
Open Jira epics for KV metrics, canary-latency UI, and Private-onboard CLI; link to this doc (owner: Tom) — target by 2029-06-22
notes: This is intentionally a tactical stitch — goal is to turn noisy asks into measurable probes. Keep language customer-facing when recruiting pilots; be explicit about data minimization. We should avoid full-bore telemetry until probes show clear ROI.
